Hanuman. The monkey god and one of the most beloved figures in Hindu mythology, revered for his unwavering devotion, courage, and loyalty.

Hanuman is the divine monkey god and devoted follower of Rama. He embodies the principle of loyalty and bhakti, devotional love, in Hindu tradition. He possesses extraordinary strength, agility, and magical powers, capable of transforming his size and leaping across vast distances.

As a central hero of the Ramayana, Hanuman performs crucial feats including the search for Sita and the destruction of Ravana's kingdom. He is depicted with a monkey's body and a noble human face. He carries a mace and wears sacred marks, symbolizing his divine nature.

Hanuman's devotion to Rama transcends the story itself. He has become a symbol of unwavering faith and surrender to the divine. He renounces all claims to personal power or reward, seeking only to serve Rama's cause and will without expectation of recognition.

He is worshipped as the ideal of celibacy, strength, courage, and discipline. Temples and festivals are dedicated to his honor throughout the Hindu world. Hanuman represents a principle that spiritual greatness does not lie in divinity itself, but in perfect devotion and obedience to a higher truth. His life exemplifies how the greatest power comes through complete dedication to serving something greater than oneself.
